sectors.note:
**TL;DR:** Defensive and interest-sensitive sectors are surging as Healthcare, Real Estate, and Consumer Defensive lead recent rank improvements, while Utilities and cyclical sectors fade.

Market breadth reveals a clear rotation toward stability, with 4 of 11 groups achieving "all-green" status (positive across weekly, monthly, quarterly, half-year, and YTD horizons). Healthcare and Consumer Defensive have both climbed 3 spots in rank over the last 5 sessions, while Real Estate gained 2 spots. Despite this defensive rotation, Energy remains the overall momentum leader with a score of 0.850.

On the downside, Utilities experienced the sharpest decline, dropping 3 spots to rank 9. Cyclicals are also losing ground, with Industrials and Basic Materials both slipping 2 spots, while Consumer Cyclical remains anchored at the bottom of the momentum spectrum.

## Strength
* **Broad Breadth:** Four out of 11 industry groups are currently "all-green," showing positive performance across all short- and long-term timeframes.
* **Top All-Green Performers:** Healthcare and Real Estate lead the all-green cohort, both sporting robust momentum scores of 0.73.
* **Financial & Defensive Support:** Financials (0.67 momentum) and Consumer Defensive (0.65 momentum) round out the structurally strongest sectors in the market.

## Movers & Momentum
* **Upward Rotation:** Consumer Defensive (+3 spots to rank 4) and Healthcare (+3 spots to rank 6) are the week's fastest-improving sectors, followed by Real Estate (+2 spots to rank 2).
* **Steepest Decliners:** Utilities fell 3 spots to rank 9 (momentum 0.22), while Industrials (rank 5) and Basic Materials (rank 7) both dropped 2 spots.
* **Momentum Extremes:** Energy remains the absolute momentum leader at 0.850 (YTD rank 1), whereas Consumer Cyclical is the primary laggard with a near-zero momentum score of 0.07 (YTD rank 11).

## Divergences
* **Stable Leadership:** No fragile "all-green" sectors or early-warning rank mismatches were detected in the data, indicating that current sector trends are well-supported by underlying momentum.

industries.note:
**TL;DR:** Defensive services and consumer electronics anchor the market's 25% "all-green" breadth, while commodities and renewables suffer sharp corrections.

Market breadth remains moderate with 36 of 144 groups holding all-green status, led by sustained strength in Consumer Electronics (0.90 momentum) and Staffing & Employment Services (0.87 momentum). Pockets of the services sector are rotating into favor, highlighted by massive weekly rank improvements in Education & Training Services (+40 spots) and Insurance Brokers (+27 spots). 

Conversely, cyclical and commodity-linked groups are fading rapidly. Silver (-45 spots) and Utilities - Renewable (-42 spots) suffered the sharpest declines this week, alongside notable pullbacks in Aluminum (-30 spots) and Semiconductors (-23 spots). 

## Strength
* **Healthy Breadth:** 36 of 144 industry groups are currently "all-green," showing positive performance across the week, month, quarter, half, and YTD.
* **Sustained Leaders:** Consumer Electronics (0.90 momentum), Staffing & Employment Services (0.87 momentum), and Publishing (0.87 momentum) demonstrate both absolute momentum leadership and sustained long-term strength.
* **Defensive Anchors:** Insurance - Reinsurance (0.79 momentum) and Insurance - Property & Casualty (0.76 momentum) maintain all-green status, supported by sustained strength in Insurance - Life.

## Movers & Momentum
* **Top Gainers:** Education & Training Services surged +40 spots to rank 60 (0.71 momentum), followed by Insurance Brokers (+27 spots to rank 87) and Travel Services (+22 spots to rank 99).
* **Sharpest Decliners:** Silver plunged -45 spots to rank 105 (0.26 momentum), while Utilities - Renewable fell -42 spots to rank 92 (0.25 momentum), and Aluminum dropped -30 spots to rank 107.
* **Momentum Extremes:** Consumer Electronics (0.902) and Oil & Gas Refining & Marketing (0.871) lead absolute momentum, while Auto Manufacturers (0.076) and Utilities - Independent Power Producers (0.080) remain the market's deepest laggards.

## Divergences
* **Fading Groups:** Several groups show high momentum but slipping short-term ranks, including Banks - Diversified (momentum 0.66, down 8 spots), Metal Fabrication (momentum 0.60, down 5 spots), and Department Stores (momentum 0.66, down 4 spots).
* **Emerging Groups:** Early-stage rank improvements with low-to-moderate momentum are appearing in Discount Stores (+13 spots, 0.50 momentum), Medical Devices (+11 spots, 0.48 momentum), and Resorts & Casinos (+9 spots, 0.47 momentum).
